entries.note: 'Not terrible' is an evaluation of quality without a shared factual threshold.
This judges what valuation would be justified, rather than predicting an actual valuation decline.

entries.test: Public departure announcements, employment histories, and company founding records would establish whether numerous prominent OpenAI alumni left to found competitors.
entries.note: The preceding sentence supplies the referent for 'those people.' Founding competitors is publicly observable.

entries.test: Contemporaneous model release timelines, comparative capability evaluations, and reporting on OpenAI–Microsoft negotiations would test the claimed competitive pace, narrowing lead, and relationship tensions.
entries.note: 'Elon' refers contextually to his AI venture. The comparisons are imprecise but have a plain competitive reading.
The antecedent is correctly identified, but 'all bullshit' does not specify a shared factual test across those different statements.
Marcus endorses only a possibility, preserving 'may.' Being the 'right CEO' is also evaluative.

entries.test: The ASU paper's methods, tested models, and out-of-distribution results would establish whether it demonstrated the stated failure to extend learned universals beyond training examples.
entries.note: The preceding paragraph supplies the meaning of 'exactly the same thing.' This is a checkable characterization of research findings.
This is a sweeping denunciation; the subsequent examples contain separate factual commitments.

entries.test: Public agent evaluations, deployment studies, and user reports would test whether poor agent performance causes widespread difficulty finding workable real-world applications.
entries.note: 'So badly that' attributes the difficulty finding applications to poor performance. The insult accompanies a substantive causal claim.

entries.test: Published studies, benchmark protocols, graph provenance, and model architecture and training disclosures would test the alleged selective reporting, benchmark manipulation, and absence of transparency.
entries.note: The closing metaphor summarizes a factual criticism of industry research practices. 'Zero transparency' is a strong claim that public disclosures can challenge.

entries.test: Public statements by previously enthusiastic technology advocates would establish whether some had begun acknowledging that AGI-in-2027 messaging was promotional rather than a substantiated timetable.
entries.note: In context, this reports a change in expressed attitudes toward a promoted timeline; it is not itself a dated forecast.

entries.test: Public evaluations across the cited model families and other contemporary LLMs would establish whether the recurring failures persisted and whether robust generalization under distribution shift had been achieved.
entries.note: 'The same problems' refers to the preceding list of reasoning, chess, vision, arithmetic, and hallucination failures. 'Never' concerns the record through publication.

entries.test: A publicly demonstrated AGI produced by scaling existing approaches alone, with documented methods and independent capability evaluations, would falsify the claim.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supports the categorical future reading. Continued failures alone cannot establish that scaling will never succeed.

entries.test: A publicly documented attention-based system attaining independently demonstrated AGI without the additional representational mechanisms Marcus says are necessary would falsify the claim.
entries.note: The surrounding paragraphs supply AGI as the target. 'Attention' is contextual shorthand for the current architectural approach, rather than a literal standalone operation.
